title: [factory-setup-agent] Sandbox amendment round 2: roles now get a real database and an app that reloads
body:
Amendment episode for sandbox report `5223262fddb6abfe`, from a builder that could not exercise its `GET /sensors` change. Artifacts are in `setup-round-*`; the trial measures the result.

## What the report described

Two separate blockers, one cause each.

1. **No database.** `DATABASE_URL` named `127.0.0.1:5432`, which is the sidecar address **on the runner**. A role's agent runs in a container on its own network (`172.30.0.0/24`), where that port is refused and `host.docker.internal:5432` times out. The `test` command exited on its database precondition and the builder's four new tests skipped — *11 passed, 11 skipped*, green while testing no database code at all.
2. **A stale app.** `bsf sandbox start --serve` runs `commands.run` on the runner once, before the agent exists, and round 1 deliberately made that non-reloading. `/openapi.json` kept listing the three original paths however many times the builder edited `app/main.py`.

Reproduced both in the setup container before changing anything: `connect_ex` on `127.0.0.1:5432` returns `ECONNREFUSED` here too.

## Why the obvious fixes do not work

- **Opening port 5432 to the agent.** Not expressible. The host-access role variant is selected by `needsHost()` and opens exactly one host port, `allow-host-ports: [8787]`, which `serveOnHost` already spends on a TCP forwarder to the app. There is no manifest field that asks for a second.
- **Swapping in SQLite.** Rejected on the report's own evidence: SQLite's `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` is second-resolution, so the one assertion the builder could not make — two consecutive POSTs get distinct `recorded_at` — would still be unmakeable.
- **Dropping the `services` entry.** It is also what makes `needsHost()` true, so removing it would cost port 8787 as well as the database.

## What changed

**`.venv/bin/sandbox-db`, written by `install`.** Checks whether anything answers at `DATABASE_URL`; if nothing does, it runs `initdb -A trust` and `pg_ctl start` on the same address from the PostgreSQL binaries already in the image. On the runner the sidecar answers first and it does nothing. `test`, `run` and `seed` all call it. The check is "does this address answer", not "am I in a container".

**`commands.run` is now `uvicorn --reload --reload-dir app`.** Round 1 dropped `--reload` on the theory that a file-watching supervisor would confuse the trial's process-group teardown. That theory was untested and wrong: replicating the trial exactly — `spawn('bash', ['-c', run], {detached: true})` then `kill(-pid, 'SIGTERM')` — the reloader and its worker both die, no survivors in `ps`.

**`WATCHFILES_FORCE_POLLING=1` added to `env`** (kind `self`). This is the one defensive rather than measured choice, and it is flagged as such in the manifest: the builder writes from a different mount namespace than the runner-side reloader watches, a single container cannot test whether inotify crosses that, and polling does not depend on the answer.

## Measured

All from a cold start, with commands read back out of the written JSON and executed rather than retyped.

|  | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `install` / `build` | exit 0; `All checks passed!`, `Success: no issues found in 7 source files` |
| `test` **in this container** | started a local 18.7 cluster, then **18 passed, 96% coverage** — was 11 passed / 11 skipped |
| `test` ×3 against one cluster | 18 passed each time, `cleared 5 row(s)` each time |
| `run` | `/docs` 200 in 1s; `/health` ok; kitchen 3/19.0/23.25/21.25; `/sensors/nope/summary` 404; celsius -400 → 422 |
| live reload | `GET /sensors` appeared in `/openapi.json` **1s** after the write and answered with rows from the database |
| two POSTs back to back | `07:17:38.358362Z` vs `07:17:38.366271Z` — distinct, the assertion the builder could not make |
| trial control | `build` and `test` both exit 127 in an empty directory |
| browser | Swagger UI renders, all four operations; one console error (the `fastapi.tiangolo.com` favicon) |

Tier stays **renders**. One bug found and fixed on the way: the first helper wrote `initdb.log` into the data directory before `initdb` ran, which `initdb` refuses.

## Worth knowing

A role's container now tests against **PostgreSQL 18.7** while the gates test against **`postgres:17-alpine`**. The suite passes on both, but version-specific SQL could pass for a builder and fail in the gates. That is recorded under `capabilities.not_exercised` with paths, along with the new entry for the app no longer running as a single non-reloading process.

Context docs updated: `runbook.md` gains a "Where your commands actually run" table and the reload/`sandbox-db` details; `history.md` gains the lessons, including not to re-drop `--reload` on round 1's reasoning. `feature-map.md` is unchanged — no code facts moved.
